chains.title: Variant creates a stronger CEBPA site in the SORT1 enhancer; CEBPA activates SORT1 in hepatocytes

links.claim: The T allele binds CEBPA more strongly than the G allele. CEBPA has its own QBiC-SELEX model at this base, not only a CEBPB surrogate: effect +2.803, z 22.63, with the T allele reaching the 98.8th percentile versus 66.0th for G. CEBPA is highly expressed in Hep 3B2.1-7 (141.33 TPM, rank 18 of 1626 TFs) and has an ENCODE ChIP-seq peak over the variant in HepG2. This establishes a CEBPA-specific in vitro allelic preference plus occupancy, though not allele-specific occupancy in vivo.

The variant lies in the distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E1374646 with DNase, H3K27ac and H3K4me3 signal, and CEBPA has a HepG2 ChIP-seq peak over the variant, supporting an active, occupied liver enhancer element.

SORT1 is the strongest gene-level link: L2G 0.99 and a liver eQTL with NES +1.27 for the T allele. CELSR2 and PSRC1 are also in the same PSRC1-CELSR2-SORT1 cluster, but SORT1 has the strongest L2G and liver eQTL support.

HepG2 is the matching biosample standing in for Hep 3B2.1-7. CEBPA is expressed in the DepMap liver cancer line and is ChIP-occupied over the variant in HepG2, making a hepatocyte-model mechanism plausible.

If the T allele increases CEBPA binding and hepatic SORT1 expression, it would be predicted to lower LDL-C and/or remnant cholesterol and reduce coronary risk; the G allele is the GWAS risk allele for high cholesterol/LDL-C. E18b cautions that CHD protection from this gene cluster may be independent of LDL-C via remnant cholesterol, so LDL-C mediation is plausible but not proven.

predictions: Allele-specific CEBPA occupancy is higher on the T allele in hepatocytes.
CEBPA knockdown reduces SORT1 expression and the T-versus-G enhancer reporter difference.
Conditioning on this base attenuates the LDL-C association, but fine-mapping alone does not distinguish CEBPA from CEBPG.
falsified_if: Allele-specific CEBPA ChIP or reporter assays show no difference between G and T at this base.
CEBPA knockdown does not affect SORT1 expression or the T-versus-G enhancer activity difference in hepatocyte models.
The LDL-C signal is fully explained by a different linked variant after conditioning on this base.

chains.title: Variant creates a stronger CEBPG site at the same SORT1 enhancer; CEBPG is an alternative CEBP-family activator

links.claim: The T allele binds CEBPG more strongly than the G allele. CEBPG has its own QBiC-SELEX model with effect +2.321 and z 26.76, and the T allele reaches the 99.4th percentile. CEBPG is expressed in Hep 3B2.1-7 (46.37 TPM, rank 103 of 1626 TFs) and has a HepG2 ChIP-seq peak over the variant. CEBP-family TFs share binding specificity, so motif preference alone does not distinguish CEBPG from CEBPA; CEBPG is a plausible alternative because it also has its own model and occupancy.
The variant lies in the active distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E1374646, and CEBPG has a HepG2 ChIP-seq peak over the variant, supporting an occupied active enhancer element.

This chain does not claim specificity to CELSR2 over SORT1. SORT1 has the strongest L2G score (0.99) and a liver eQTL with NES +1.27 for the T allele; CELSR2 and PSRC1 are additional genes in the same cluster.
CEBPG is expressed in the DepMap liver cancer line and is ChIP-occupied over the variant in HepG2, supporting the HepG2/Hep 3B2.1-7 liver-cell context.

If CEBPG mediates the T-allele effect and raises SORT1, the direction would match the T-allele SORT1 eQTL and the G risk allele for high cholesterol/LDL-C. The same caveat applies: E18b suggests CHD protection may be independent of LDL-C via remnant cholesterol, so phenotypic mediation through CEBPG is inferred rather than shown.

predictions: Allele-specific CEBPG occupancy is higher on the T allele in hepatocytes.
CEBPG knockdown reduces SORT1 expression and the T-versus-G enhancer reporter difference more than CEBPA knockdown.
CEBPA knockdown leaves the allele-specific effect largely intact.
falsified_if: Allele-specific CEBPG ChIP or reporter assays show no difference between G and T at this base.
CEBPG knockdown does not affect SORT1 expression or the T-versus-G enhancer activity difference in liver-derived cells.
CEBPA occupancy and perturbation fully explain the allele-specific effect, leaving no independent CEBPG contribution.

chains.title: Variant alters MLX binding; MLX represses SORT1

links.claim: The G allele binds MLX more strongly than the T allele. MLX has its own QBiC-SELEX model with effect -0.496 and z -15.37, and the G allele reaches the 99.4th percentile versus 82.1th for T. MLX is expressed in Hep 3B2.1-7 (57.97 TPM, rank 73 of 1626 TFs) and has a HepG2 ChIP-seq peak over the variant. This supports an MLX allelic preference plus occupancy, but not allele-specific occupancy in vivo.
The variant lies in the active distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E1374646, and MLX ChIP occupancy over the variant supports a functional element in HepG2.
SORT1 has the strongest L2G score (0.99) and a liver eQTL with NES +1.27 for the T allele, linking this variant to SORT1 expression.
MLX is expressed in the DepMap liver cancer line and is ChIP-occupied over the variant in HepG2, supporting a liver-cell context.

If MLX represses SORT1, the G risk allele would bind MLX more, lower SORT1, and raise LDL-C/remnant cholesterol, while the T allele would lose repression and raise SORT1. This matches the GWAS risk allele G and the T-allele SORT1 eQTL direction, but the repression premise itself is not established by the cited evidence.

predictions: Allele-specific MLX occupancy is higher on the G allele in hepatocytes.
MLX knockdown increases SORT1 expression and increases G-allele enhancer activity.
If MLX is an activator rather than a repressor, the phenotype direction reverses and this chain is falsified.
falsified_if: Allele-specific MLX ChIP or reporter assays show no difference between G and T at this base.
MLX knockdown does not change SORT1 expression or the allele-specific enhancer activity.
MLX behaves as an activator in this context, reversing the predicted direction.

grades_v0.reason: HepG2 ChIP gives occupancy over the variant, but not allele-specific occupancy. The QBiC-SELEX signal for CEBPA is from a CIS-BP-mapped CEBPB model, not CEBPA's own model, so the allele-specific binding change is indirect and TF identity is not established.
E03 places the variant in dELS EH38E1374646 with DNase, H3K27ac, and H3K4me3 signal, and E04/E21 show a HepG2 ChIP peak over the variant, directly supporting an active enhancer element.

E16 gives SORT1 L2G 0.99 and E17 gives a liver SORT1 eQTL with NES +1.27 for the T allele, directly linking this variant to SORT1 expression; SORT1 is the strongest gene-level assignment among the nearby genes.
E04 explicitly uses HepG2 as the matching biosample standing in for Hep 3B2.1-7, and E21 shows CEBPA expression in the DepMap liver cancer line plus ChIP occupancy in HepG2.

The GWAS risk allele G and the T-allele SORT1 eQTL direction are consistent with the proposed direction, but no CEBPA perturbation shows that CEBPA mediates SORT1 expression or LDL-C/MI. E18b also states that protection from this gene cluster is independent of LDL-C, contrary to the simple LDL-C mediation claimed.

CEBPG has its own QBiC-SELEX model with a large alt-allele effect (z 26.76, effect +2.321), a strong alt-allele site, and a HepG2 ChIP peak over the variant (E20); occupancy is not allele-specific, but both occupancy and a TF-specific in vitro binding change are present.
The variant lies in EH38E1374646 dELS with active chromatin marks (E03), and CEBPG has a HepG2 ChIP peak over the variant (E20), supporting an occupied active enhancer element.
CELSR2 and PSRC1 do have eQTL/L2G support, but SORT1 has the stronger L2G score and liver eQTL. The evidence does not support the claim that this enhancer links to CELSR2/PSRC1 rather than SORT1.
CEBPG is expressed in the DepMap liver cancer line and has a HepG2 ChIP peak over the variant (E20), matching the HepG2-for-Hep3B liver cancer context.

The T-allele direction for CELSR2/PSRC1 expression and the G risk allele are directionally consistent, but there is no CEBPG perturbation showing that CEBPG changes CELSR2/PSRC1 expression or LDL-C/MI, and E18b indicates CHD protection independent of LDL-C.

MLX has its own QBiC-SELEX model with a ref-allele effect (z -15.37, effect -0.496), a strong ref-allele site, and a HepG2 ChIP peak over the variant (E22); allele-specific occupancy is not shown, but occupancy plus a TF-specific binding change is present.
E03 assigns the variant to EH38E1374646 dELS with active chromatin marks, and E22 shows MLX ChIP occupancy over the variant in HepG2, supporting a functional element.
E16 gives SORT1 the strongest L2G score (0.99), and E17 shows a liver SORT1 eQTL with NES +1.27 for the T allele, directly linking the variant to SORT1 expression.
MLX is expressed in the DepMap liver cancer line and has a HepG2 ChIP peak over the variant (E22), supporting the liver cancer cell context.

The GWAS/eQTL directions can fit a repressor model, but no evidence cited shows that MLX represses SORT1 or that MLX occupancy changes LDL-C or myocardial infarction risk. The repression premise is unestablished.

RXRA has ChIP occupancy over the variant in HepG2 and liver, but its best QBiC-SELEX model here is a CIS-BP-mapped NR2F2 model, not RXRA's own model. NR2F2 and other NR2F-family factors also bind, so allele-specific RXRA binding is not established.
The variant is in EH38E1374646 dELS with active chromatin marks (E03), and RXRA ChIP occupancy over the variant in HepG2/liver supports a nuclear-receptor-occupied enhancer element.
E16 gives SORT1 L2G 0.99 and E17 shows the liver SORT1 eQTL with NES +1.27 for the T allele, directly supporting SORT1 as the linked gene.
RXRA is expressed in the DepMap liver cancer line and is ChIP-occupied in HepG2 and liver (E12, E29), supporting a liver-cell context.

The T-allele SORT1 eQTL and G risk allele are directionally consistent, but RXRA-specific mediation is unsupported because the binding evidence is NR2F2-model-based and no RXRA perturbation shows effects on SORT1 or LDL-C/MI.

grades_final.reason: E35 provides a CEBPA own-model QBiC-SELEX change in the stated direction (alt/T effect +2.803, z 22.63, alt site 98.8th vs ref 66.0th), and E21/E04 provide HepG2 ChIP occupancy over the variant. CEBPA is expressed in the matching DepMap line. This meets occupancy plus allele-specific binding change.

E03 supports a dELS cCRE at the variant with DNase/H3K27ac/H3K4me3, but the reported z-scores are maxima across ENCODE biosamples, not HepG2-specific. HepG2 ChIP occupancy supports an occupied element, but active enhancer marks in the matching liver-cell context are not directly shown.

E16 gives SORT1 L2G 0.99 and E17 gives a liver SORT1 eQTL with T-allele NES +1.27, directly linking this variant to SORT1 expression in liver. Direction is consistent with T-allele CEBPA binding gain and SORT1 activation.
E04 states HepG2 is the matching biosample standing in for Hep 3B2.1-7, and E35/E21 show CEBPA expression in the DepMap liver line plus HepG2 ChIP occupancy over the variant.

GWAS and eQTL evidence support the variant-phenotype direction (G risk for high cholesterol/LDLC; T increases SORT1), and E18b supports a protective PSRC1-CELSR2-SORT1/remnant-cholesterol axis. However, CEBPA-mediated SORT1 activation causing LDL-C/CHD change is inferred, not shown by perturbation; E18b also notes CHD protection may be LDL-C-independent, and one LDL record in E15 reports a T effect allele.

E20 provides CEBPG own-model QBiC-SELEX support for stronger alt/T binding (effect +2.321, z 26.76, alt 99.4th percentile) and HepG2 ChIP occupancy over the variant. CEBPG is expressed in the matching DepMap line, so occupancy plus a directional binding change are present.

The variant is in the dELS EH38E1374646 and CEBPG occupies it in HepG2, but E03's DNase/H3K27ac/H3K4me3 scores are maxima over biosamples, not demonstrated for HepG2. Occupancy is shown; active enhancer status in the matching cell type is indirect.

For the stated target SORT1, E16 gives L2G 0.99 and E17 gives a liver eQTL with T-allele NES +1.27. The claim explicitly does not assert CELSR2 specificity, and CELSR2/PSRC1 are also in the same cluster. The chain ID/title mention of CELSR2 does not match the SORT1 target, but the gene-step claim as written is supported for SORT1.
E04 establishes HepG2 as the stand-in biosample, and E20 shows CEBPG expression in the DepMap Hep 3B2.1-7 line plus HepG2 ChIP occupancy over the variant.

The genetic direction is consistent with T-allele SORT1 increase and G risk, but there is no evidence that CEBPG activates SORT1 or mediates the phenotype. The phenotype link is therefore an inference from GWAS/eQTL/gene-cluster literature, not a demonstrated CEBPG mechanism.

E22 provides an MLX own-model QBiC-SELEX change in the stated direction (ref/G binds more; effect -0.496, z -15.37, ref 99.4th vs alt 82.1st percentile) and HepG2 ChIP occupancy over the variant. MLX is expressed in the matching DepMap line.

E03 places the variant in dELS EH38E1374646 and E22 shows MLX occupancy in HepG2, but the histone/DNase support is reported as maxima across ENCODE biosamples, not HepG2-specific. Active enhancer status in the relevant liver-cell context is therefore indirect.

E16 and E17 directly link the variant to SORT1 expression (L2G 0.99; liver eQTL T-allele NES +1.27). This supports the variant-SORT1 gene link, though it does not by itself establish that MLX represses SORT1.
E04 establishes HepG2 as the matching stand-in for Hep 3B2.1-7, and E22 shows MLX expression in the DepMap liver line plus HepG2 ChIP occupancy over the variant.

The direction can be made consistent only if MLX represses SORT1: G binds MLX more, would lower SORT1, and G is the risk allele while T increases SORT1. But the repression premise is not established by any cited assay, and no perturbation links MLX activity to SORT1 or LDL-C/CHD. The phenotype link is therefore conditional and indirect.

checks.why: This determines whether the reported QBiC-SELEX change is from CEBPA's own model or a CEBPB surrogate; if it is only a surrogate, the CEBPA binding link remains weak and CEBPG may be the better CEBP-family candidate.
This clarifies whether RXRA has its own QBiC-SELEX model at this variant or is only covered through the NR2F2-mapped model, which is central to distinguishing RXRA from NR2F2.

This would find any perturbation or reporter evidence that CEBPA regulates SORT1 in liver cells; absence of such evidence would substantially weaken the highest-probability chain's phenotypic mediation.

next_experiment: Cheapest separating experiment: in HepG2 (and ideally a hepatocyte line matched to the liver eQTL context), knock down CEBPA and CEBPG separately by siRNA and measure SORT1 mRNA by qPCR. The CEBPA_SORT1_activation chain predicts CEBPA knockdown lowers SORT1 while CEBPG knockdown has little effect; the CEBPG chain predicts the opposite. This is low cost and directly separates the top two chains.
